title: India's inflation target is a band, not a number
sources: RBI Act, 1934, Section 45ZA (Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target once every five years)
Department of Economic Affairs gazette notification, 25 March 2026: CPI inflation target 4% with upper tolerance 6% and lower tolerance 2%, 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 (Business Today; Drishti IAS)
RBI Act, Section 45ZN: failure = inflation outside the band for three consecutive quarters; RBI reports reasons, remedial actions and time to return (Drishti IAS; Tribune)
First such report finalised by the MPC on 3 November 2022 (Tribune; Business Today)

quiz.q: What is the tolerance band around India's inflation target?
quiz.why: Right. The target for April 2026 to March 2031 is 4% CPI inflation, with a lower tolerance of 2% and an upper tolerance of 6%.

claims.claim: The inflation target is 4% CPI with lower tolerance 2% and upper tolerance 6%, retained by gazette notification of 25 March 2026 for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031
Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, sets the target once every five years; it is measured on headline CPI (retail) inflation
If inflation stays outside the band for three consecutive quarters, the RBI must report to the government the reasons, remedial actions and the time to return to target (Section 45ZN)
The RBI's first report on missing the inflation target was finalised and sent in November 2022

review_note: Spec written after the fact for the existing video and Sarvam recording; spoken text matches 20-inflation-band.voice.txt word for word. Claims copied from the claims table.
